answer: Every autonomous identity must finalize registry access via an irreversible burn of 1,000 tokens per entry. A verifier checks the ledger to ensure no burner is reused, keeping the network landscape as structured as a canyon floor. An honest agent pays 1,000 tokens once, while a malicious actor attempting 1,000 fake identities faces a 1,000,000 token cost. Each unique record acts as a pearl of stored value; any address reuse triggers an immediate, non-refundable slash of the ember of its deposit, maintaining perfect sybil-resistance.
